customManagers.description: The screenshots workflow runs the Playwright container whose browsers belong to @playwright/test in apps/frontend/e2e/package.json; e2e/screens/files.test.ts fails while the two differ.

packageRules.description: Never bump PyExifTool. Pinned to 0.4.9; 0.5.x breaks metadata extraction.

Never auto-bump these: hdbscan and timezonefinder have Windows and arm64 wheels built by prebuilt-wheels.yml and pinned by URL in apps/backend/requirements.txt next to the PyPI pin. Renovate would move the PyPI line alone. Bump every line together by hand and re-run the workflow.

ruff is pinned in four places that must move together: required-version in apps/backend/pyproject.toml, requirements.dev.txt, .pre-commit-config.yaml and .github/workflows/lint-backend.yml (not seen by Renovate). A minor ruff release can change the default rules and the formatter: 0.16.3 reports 687 findings on a tree 0.15.22 passes and reformats Markdown code blocks. Bump it by hand together with the fixes and a regenerated apps/backend/ruff-baseline.toml (scripts/ruff_baseline.py --update); api/tests/infra/test_ruff_pins.py fails while the four pins differ.

Never bump requires-python in apps/backend/pyproject.toml. It is the supported range (floor = the oldest Python a build runs, 3.14 for the images and the Windows standalone build; ceiling = the first Python a dependency lacks wheels for, 3.15 for onnxruntime), not a dependency; api/tests/infra/test_python_versions.py keeps it in sync with the images and workflows. Renovate once proposed >=3.15,<3.16, which moved ruff's target version to 3.15 and failed the lint.

Type checking (apps/backend/scripts/typecheck.py). A mypy or stub release changes the reported errors, so the PR has to fix them (or regenerate mypy-baseline.txt with --update) before it can merge: one group, never automerged. djangorestframework-stubs 3.18.1 declares mypy<2.4.

The root package.json is the npm workspace for apps/mobile and packages/*, and pins Expo, expo-router, React and zod to move in lockstep with apps/mobile. packages/api-client is installed through this workspace, so its tooling updates land here too, although the web app also compiles it (its zod and React Query move with the shared client runtime group below). Exact root paths, so apps/frontend and apps/docs manifests are not caught.

Expo SDK 57 pins these: expo's bundledNativeModules.json names the exact version (or patch range) of every native module it was built and tested with, and react, react-dom, react-test-renderer, @types/react, jest-expo and react-native must match each other exactly (jest-expo hard-fails otherwise, and its peer ranges break the lockfile update). Minor and patch bumps inside an SDK are not ours to pick. Move them only when moving to a new SDK, with `npx expo install --fix` in apps/mobile (then mirror expo, expo-router, react, react-dom and the overrides in the root package.json). SDK majors still come through as major PRs.

Majors of the mobile test, styling and lint tooling are tied to the Expo SDK, not to their own release cycle, so they wait for the next SDK upgrade (#2148 bundled them and could not merge). jest-expo 57 runs on Jest 29 (jest 30 and @types/jest 30 do not fit), Testing Library for React Native 14 needs React >= 19.3 while SDK 57 ships 19.2.3 (and its async API is a test rewrite), Tailwind CSS 4 needs NativeWind 5 (react-native-css-interop accepts Tailwind 3 only), eslint-config-expo 57's plugins support ESLint 9 only, and SDK 57 bundles react-native-gesture-handler ~2.32 (the root overrides pin it too). They are listed on the Dependency Dashboard and come as one PR only when ticked there: tick it during an Expo SDK upgrade. SDK-versioned packages (expo, jest-expo, eslint-config-expo, babel-preset-expo) are left out on purpose, their majors are the SDK upgrade itself. packages/api-client is not matched: it has its own ESLint 10 setup.
Deploy updates are never built by PR CI (the image workflows run on push to dev only), so they must not automerge.
The k8s manifests pin release tags and a Postgres major by hand; a Postgres major refuses to start on an existing data volume. Update them manually with a documented migration.
A new Ubuntu release swaps the distro Python under the backend base image (resolute = 26.04 ships 3.14; the prebuilt wheels are cp314). Move between LTS releases by hand after a test build.
The proxy stays on nginx's stable branch, whose minor versions are even (1.30, 1.32). Odd minors are mainline: the 1.31 tag is the same image as mainline.

The Python a workflow sets up is a target, not a tool to keep current: the Windows standalone build and the prebuilt wheels are cp314, pinned by URL in apps/backend/requirements.txt. Renovate counts 3.14 -> 3.15 as a minor update, which the github-actions group automerges. Move it by hand together with requires-python, the base image and the wheels.

Both compose files pin pgautoupgrade to a Postgres major (18-alpine). A new major upgrades every compose install's database on its next pull, so it comes as its own pull request, never grouped and never automerged, and ships with release-note instructions (back up first).
A Postgres major needs pg_upgrade or dump/restore on existing volumes. Never bump it automatically.

nwsapi is pinned to 2.2.13 through resolutions in apps/frontend/package.json: 2.2.28 makes jsdom's selector matching 4-6x slower, and the ModalTagEdit tests time out at vitest's 5 s default. Check a newer release's test timings by hand before moving the pin.
typescript-eslint 8 supports TypeScript < 6.1 only; a newer TypeScript fails lint before anything else runs.
Docusaurus, React and MDX majors in the docs site have to move together (Docusaurus pins its React and @mdx-js/react peer ranges), so keep them in one separate PR instead of the docs group.
Frontend majors are split so the safe ones can merge alone. React 19 and Mantine 9 have to ship together (with recharts, which only @mantine/charts uses). Both landed in #2171.

packages/api-client's zod schemas and React Query hooks run inside both apps, on each app's copy, so zod and React Query move in one PR across the web app, the mobile app, the package and the root workspace pin; scripts/check-shared-deps.mjs (run by lint-frontend.yml and api-client.yml) fails while a consumer is outside the package's peer range or the apps' zod majors differ. React is left out: the Expo SDK pins the mobile app's React (rule above).
PR CI does not run the Playwright suite, so keep its updates apart from the app's.
@playwright/test and the Playwright container tag in the screenshots workflow move in one PR.
